messages:
Amy (CS): Heads-up - customer AcmeAnalytics opened a billing escalation. They say Dedicated shows 720 reserved GPU hours charged this month but their usage dashboard shows ~120 active hours and a lot of burst credits. They believe we're double-billing reserved hours + burst.
Jordan (SRE): @Amy can you paste the invoice ID or account id? need to correlate with capacity allocation logs.
Amy (CS): acct: acme-12233, invoice: INV-2026-03-09-ACME. Customer claims billing line 'Dedicated Reserved Hours' is 720 and 'Burst Usage' 300, but their token usage is low. They attached screenshots.
Marie Chen: pulling invoice now. On first glance reserved hours are prorated commit for the month. Are they on a monthly reserved capacity plan or did they scale down?
Amy (CS): They had reserved pool of 1x A100 for entire month; then on 03/10 they requested scale-down to 0.5 pool for planned maintenance, and they used burst capacity on 03/12-03/14 for a spike. They say our dashboard shows 120 GPU-hours total.
Alex M.: quick note: dashboard token->GPU-hour mapping can be lossy. We meter GPU-hours on the infra side (alloc time * nodes) while customer-facing token latency table is token-based throughput. If a machine was reserved but idle, infra still records reserved allocation.
Jordan (SRE): steps I'll run: 1) check dedicated allocator logs for acme-12233 between 2026-03-01 and 2026-03-31. 2) check autoscale events and burst allocations. 3) compute GPU-hour billing from allocation timeline.
billing-bot: Billing snapshot for acct acme-12233 loaded: reserved_commit=720h, burst_charged=300h, credits_applied=0, sla_credit_pending=false.
Marie Chen: @Jordan can you confirm whether scale-down request on 03/10 actually changed the reserved commit or just reduced running capacity? We've had cases where reserved commitment stays until end of term even if pool size is reduced.
Jordan (SRE): Looking at allocator: on 2026-03-10 09:12 UTC, user requested pool_size=0.5, but the reserved_contract_id=R-ACME-2026-01 remained. The system created a transient scaling operation but did not modify the reserved commit (expected behavior). Running nodes dropped from 1 to 0.5 for 15 days; allocator still reports reserved capacity active for billing.
Amy (CS): So likely they were billed for full reserved commit (contract) + burst usage on top. Customer expected prorating when they scaled down.
Marie Chen: Contract terms: reserved capacity is a commitment; unless they renegotiated the commit we cannot automatically prorate. We can offer goodwill SLA credit. What's the magnitude?
Jordan (SRE): Computed infra-hours: reserved_commit=720h billed, actual node runtime computed from allocator: 120.3h running, burst_allocations sum to 300.1h. That matches their dashboard numbers ~120 running + 300 burst. Billing = reserved_commit (720) + burst (300) - credits (0) = 1020h charged.
Alex M.: note for product: dashboard should show 'reserved commit vs running hours' separately and highlight when contract still active. Right now UI hides reserved commits which confuses customers.
Amy (CS): Customer is pretty upset; asked for SLA credits and an explanation. They thought scale-down implies reduced commit. Can we propose a remediation?
Marie Chen: Options: 1) explain contract terms, offer 10% goodwill credit on reserved portion; 2) escalate to finance for one-time contract amendment and prorate last 20 days; 3) offer next-month credit equal to burst hours. Which is acceptable?
Jordan (SRE): From a technical standpoint, logs show behavior is correct per current implementation. Recommend UX + docs fix. For immediate customer calm-down prefer option 1 or 2.
Amy (CS): I'll offer option 1 in first reply and ask for time to investigate deeper. Also request legal if they push for contract change.
Marie Chen: I'll pre-authorize a 10% credit on reserved hours if CS sets it as goodwill. If they escalate, we can re-open for finance sign-off.
Amy (CS): Replying to customer now: "Thanks — we found that your reserved contract (R-ACME-2026-01) remained in effect; billing applied the full committed hours plus burst usage. We're sorry for the confusion — we can issue a 10% goodwill credit on the reserved portion while we investigate possible contract adjustments. We'll follow up with detailed allocation logs and a breakdown. For transparency, can you confirm the exact timestamps when you expected the commit to be reduced?" :pray:
Jordan (SRE): FYI I'm attaching allocator slice and a short repro: ```# repro steps to pull allocation timeline
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $SRE_KEY" "https://internal-api.redwood/v1/allocator/allocations?account=acme-12233&start=2026-03-01&end=2026-03-31" | jq '.allocations[] | {ts, node_type, state, hours}' ```
Amy (CS): Thanks everyone. I'll CC finance/ops if they respond. Marking thread as high priority.
Marie Chen: Filed internal follow-up ticket FIN-ACME-12233 for possible invoice adjustment.
Alex M.: Logging a product issue: PROD-UI-761 to surface reserved commit and contract ID on the customer dashboard.
Amy (CS): Customer acknowledged the 10% offer and asked for the allocation logs and invoice line-by-line. Jordan / Marie can you send the logs to me so I can attach?
Jordan (SRE): Attaching a sanitized CSV of allocation timeline to the ticket now.
Amy (CS): Closing loop with customer: sent logs + draft invoice adjustment note. Will update here after finance reply. :white_check_mark:
